_note: Circulation milestone words for the box under the date (Wire Service script) and scripts/milestone_post.py. {N} = the milestone, {NEXT} = the next one. No em-dashes.
mine: You are copy No. {N}! Bragging rights are yours.
next: Next stop: {NEXT}. Help us get there:
fine: Total Circulation counts copies of today's paper read at nevadacitynugget.com since Oct. 30, 2026, one per phone or computer a day. No names, nothing added.

milestones.alt: A bundle of newspapers tied with red twine and a tag reading 500
milestones.head: Five Hundred Copies, and Not One Landed in a Puddle
milestones.deck: The Nugget has now been read {N} times since we started counting. Our paperboy, who is entirely imaginary, has been given the afternoon off.

milestones.alt: A parade cannon firing confetti and stars
milestones.head: One Thousand Copies! Somebody Fire the Cannon!
milestones.deck: We would fire one down Broad Street to celebrate, but we suspect that takes a Conditional Use Permit. Kindly accept this drawing of a cannon instead.

milestones.head: Fifteen Hundred, and the Counting Room Needs a Nap
milestones.deck: The counting room reports {N} copies read. The counting room is one very small computer, and it would like to discuss a raise.

milestones.alt: A coffee cup steaming on the morning paper
milestones.head: Two Thousand Copies, Most of Them Over Coffee
milestones.deck: Two thousand times somebody opened the Nugget. We picture half of them over coffee and at least one during a council meeting. We won't tell.

milestones.alt: A row of Gold Rush storefronts and a steeple under a banner reading 3,000
milestones.head: Three Thousand Copies, About One for Every Soul in Town
milestones.deck: Nevada City counted a little over 3,100 residents in the 2020 Census. Copies aren't people, and the flatlanders are padding our numbers, but we will take the comparison.

milestones.alt: A miner's gold pan full of gold nuggets
milestones.head: Four Thousand Copies: Still Gold in These Hills
milestones.deck: Panning for news keeps paying out. {N} copies read, and not one claim jumper in sight.

milestones.alt: A brass cornet with a red pennant and musical notes
milestones.head: Five Thousand! Strike Up the Band!
milestones.deck: {N} copies read. In 1941 that would have been a mountain of newsprint. This time it cost not one tree, so the band plays on.

milestones.alt: A tall top hat with a red band reading 7,500
milestones.head: Seventy-Five Hundred, Which Fits on a Hatband (a Tall One)
milestones.deck: We checked whether {N} fits on a hatband. It does, on a top hat. (Our publisher sells hats on Broad Street, so we had one handy.)

milestones.head: Ten Thousand. Hold the Front Page.
milestones.deck: Ten thousand copies read since we started counting. We would stop the presses to celebrate, but we have no presses, so we stopped the coffee pot instead. Briefly.

beyond.alt: A laurel wreath around a red star
beyond.head: {N} Copies, and Still Free Every Morning
beyond.deck: Still daily, still free, still set like it's 1941. Thank you for reading, and for passing us along.

beyond.alt: A laurel wreath around a red star
beyond.head: {N} Copies Read. We Remain Unreasonably Pleased.
beyond.deck: Another milestone for a small paper in a small town. The counting room has asked to lie down.

beyond.alt: A laurel wreath around a red star
beyond.head: {N} Copies, Townsfolk and Flatlanders Alike
beyond.deck: Locals, visitors, and everyone just passing through on Highway 49: thank you, every one of you.
